segments.title: Chương 15: 0015【Hồi cấp hai tôi từng chém người thật】
segments.content:
An unknown amount of time passed, and the bus stopped in another small town. The female ticket seller shouted at the top of her lungs, "Train station, going to the train station..."

Chen Guiliang pointed out the window, "This is my town."

"A historic tourist town?"

Bian Guanyue stuck her head out the window and saw an antique-style archway up ahead, with rows of late-Qing dynasty architecture to the side.

Chen Guiliang said, "Although it's a historic tourist town, the development isn't great... Forget it, I won't speak ill of my hometown. They're also limited by objective conditions."

Bian Guanyue was already tired of being on the bus and was eager to chat with someone. "Did you go to middle school in this town?"

"No, this is the town center school. I went to the township center school," Chen Guiliang explained. "Although the township was merged into the town, and the township government and police station were all eliminated, the township center school was kept. It's poorer and more remote there. That year, I was the only one in the entire township to get into Number Two High School."

"You were the only one?" Bian Guanyue found herself talking more and more. "That's really impressive. You must have studied very diligently."

Chen Guiliang shook his head. "I wasn't diligent. I loved to play ever since I was a kid. I went to elementary school in the village, and the whole school just had two teachers who took turns teaching."

Bian Guanyue couldn't quite figure it out. "Only two teachers for the whole school, so how often did they enroll new students?"

"Every three years. If you missed first grade at age 6, you could only wait until you were 9 to start. If you really couldn't wait, you could join an existing class," Chen Guiliang said with a smile. "I was lucky, just the right age to enroll."

Bian Guanyue found it hard to imagine. "It's almost like the mountain village schools on TV."

Chen Guiliang reminisced about his childhood, "It was actually okay, much better than the truly deep mountains. I was mischievous and made trouble since I was young, never took class notes, and never did homework. But I was always involved in any troublemaking, I even peed in someone's well once. Hehe, but I always got first place in the whole school on every exam!"

"You sound pretty proud of yourself." Bian Guanyue looked at him with contempt for peeing in a well.

Chen Guiliang said with a sigh, "But that didn't last. When I was in fifth grade, the village school collapsed in the rain. Luckily, it was a weekend, so no one was crushed. All the students were transferred to the open-air playground for half a year of classes, under a simple shed put up for shelter."

"The conditions were that bad?" Bian Guanyue asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "We held on at the playground for half a year, and for sixth grade, we went to the township school early. Don't look down on the township for being poor; to us village kids, the township was like a big city. The students who lived around the township market looked down on us village kids. Haha, but they actually had rural household registrations too."

Bian Guanyue suddenly felt that Chen Guiliang was very pitiful.

Chen Guiliang said, "Back then, I was often bullied by the township students. I fought with them almost every day. After fighting for half a year, my grades slipped quite a bit, but I fought until no one in the school dared to mess with me. If I couldn't beat the older students, I'd bite them. If I couldn't bite them, I'd throw rocks at them."

Bian Guanyue grew more and more curious. "And then?"

"Later, 'Young and Dangerous' became popular, and hooligans started appearing in the township," Chen Guiliang said with a grin. "I stole a pass from a hooligan and blocked his shot right in front of the girls. Guess what that hooligan did?"

"The hooligan beat you up?" Bian Guanyue asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "More than ten of them waited for me at the school gate after school. A classmate tipped me off, and I was so scared I climbed over the wall to escape. They chased me for several li before I got away."

Bian Guanyue was surprised. "Doesn't the school do anything? Does the school not have security guards? How can they let hooligans come into the school to play basketball?"

Chen Guiliang said, "They couldn't even pay the teachers' salaries, so where would they get the money to hire security guards? I remember during the make-up classes in the third-year middle school holidays, half the students didn't pay the fees. The head teacher's tone was almost begging when he said: The teachers haven't been paid for over half a year, and we're counting on your make-up class fees to get by."

Bian Guanyue found it hard to understand why there would be teachers who didn't get paid.

This matter couldn't be discussed in detail; it was like that in many places across the country in those years.

"Did you call the police? Were those hooligans caught?" Bian Guanyue felt like she was listening to a story.

Chen Guiliang said, "The head teacher helped me call the police. They took a statement, but they didn't catch the main culprits. A few of the hooligan leaders got wind of it and ran off, and the ones left were all small fry. Plus, no harm was done, so they just called their parents in for a scolding and that was it. Two months later, a few of the hooligan leaders came back. More than ten of them cornered me on the road with knives."

Bian Guanyue was getting a little nervous listening and unconsciously clenched her fists. "You ran again?"

"There was nowhere to run."

Chen Guiliang shook his head.

"Actually, those hooligans just wanted to scare me, to make me kneel and beg for mercy and crawl between their legs. Their watermelon knives weren't even sharpened. At most, they would have just beaten me up again."

"But I couldn't handle being scared like that back then. I really thought they were going to hack me to death. In a panic, I ran to a fruit stand by the road. I grabbed a sharpened watermelon knife, held my schoolbag in my left hand as a shield, and swung the watermelon knife in my right hand wildly."

"One against thirteen. In the end, it was me chasing them and hacking at them. My mind was a complete blank. I don't even know how I stopped. Four of the hooligans ended up in the hospital. One of them lost so much blood he almost died."

Bian Guanyue exclaimed, "You're making up a story to fool me, right?"

"Haha, yes, I'm just fooling you." Chen Guiliang ended the story with a laugh.

The more Chen Guiliang said this, the more Bian Guanyue felt it was true.

The end of the story was very simple.

It was self-defense, and it didn't even delay his high school entrance exams.

The relatives of the injured were still making a fuss and demanding compensation, but Chen Guiliang's family didn't give them a single cent.

Because Chen Guiliang's father, while working as a migrant worker in the south, was tricked by a fellow townsman into jointly subcontracting a small project. The townsman took the final payment and ran off, leaving Chen Guiliang's father with all the unpaid wages.

The workers who were owed money were also all fellow townsmen. Chen Guiliang's parents could only pay them back slowly, and they were heavily in debt for many years and couldn't return home.

The moment they returned home, it would be filled with people demanding their wages!

Ever since that incident of hacking people, Chen Guiliang came to understand a principle: to avoid being bullied, you have to be more ruthless than the bad guys.

From then on, he loved to fight for justice, liked to meddle in other people's business, and foolishly thought of himself as a hero.

Naive!

But passionate.

Even his choice to major in journalism in college and become an undercover reporter after graduation was influenced by the hacking incident in middle school. He feared nothing, thinking he was a savior.

Until reality taught him one lesson after another.

The blood has not cooled, but the dream is no more.

The bus started moving again without any warning, and the female ticket seller once again got into a shouting match with a passenger.

As the bus drove over a stone arch bridge, Chen Guiliang looked at the fruit stand at the end of the bridge, "Heh, this fruit seller is still here."

Bian Guanyue looked closely, "You grabbed the watermelon knife from his stand?"

Chen Guiliang said cockily, "One man, one knife, I chased a group of hooligans from this end of the bridge to the other."

This story would sound very childish to an adult.

But it was just right for a high school student.

Bian Guanyue remembered it firmly and felt that Chen Guiliang had a certain legendary air about him.

Chen Guiliang had other stories too.

They were too dark, not suitable for telling a girl, and also liable to get this book 404'd.

Around the year 2000, public order was just that chaotic.

Growing up in such an environment without his parents to guide him, it would be strange if Chen Guiliang's personality wasn't extreme.

Fortunately, he was more Zen-like now.

"Middle school was so chaotic, how did you get into Number Two High School?" Bian Guanyue became more and more curious about Chen Guiliang.

Chen Guiliang said in a humble-bragging way, "The material in middle school is too simple. You just have to listen in class normally, and at most, memorize some politics and history after class. For my high school entrance exam, I only lost a few points on each of the Chinese, math, and English sections. I got full marks on all the other subjects."

Bian Guanyue couldn't help but roll her eyes.

So infuriating!

Chen Guiliang winked, "Have you noticed you're talking more?"

Bian Guanyue was taken aback, then immediately reverted to her cool demeanor, turning her face toward the window without a word.

Chen Guiliang laughed, "That's right, I like you when you're all cold and icy."

Bian Guanyue said angrily, "Give me back my MP3 player!"

"My mistake." Chen Guiliang apologized sincerely.

"Hmph!"

Bian Guanyue turned her face to the window again, leaving Chen Guiliang with the back of her head.

Well, and a ponytail.

Chen Guiliang really wanted to grab that ponytail to see how it felt.

But Bian Guanyue was thinking to herself: This person is so annoying, even more annoying than Li Jun!

Chen Guiliang continued to tease her, "Alright, smile a little. Have you forgotten all your troubles now?"

Hearing this, Bian Guanyue turned back and looked at him suspiciously.

Could it be that this guy said so much just now only to cheer her up and make her forget about what happened today?

It seemed she really wasn't dwelling on it anymore.

Chen Guiliang smiled, "There's no obstacle in the world that can't be overcome. I managed to come out of that quagmire alive and kicking. What's so sad about your little problems? Don't tell me it has to do with family. I haven't seen my parents in seven years, and I still live a relaxed and happy life every day."

Bian Guanyue's curiosity was piqued again. "How come you haven't seen your parents in seven years?"

"I can't be the only one talking. You have to trade your own story for it." Chen Guiliang's true motive was revealed; this was his real goal.

As long as the other person was willing to share a secret, he would have blasted an opening in their mental fortress.

He might even be able to conquer it directly!

But Bian Guanyue hesitated. She didn't like to talk about those things.

(The money-making part you all want is coming soon. What's the rush? The main character has only been reborn for a week. He can't just skip class to start a business. Taking action on the weekend is already very fast.)

No, what we're anxious about now is thirty thousand words of updates a day!! As long as the word count is high, who cares if you're making money or hitting on girls.
